name: Orphenadrine

similar.name: Medifoxamine
problems: Pulled from the market in France and Morocco, first in 1999 — for liver harm

similar.name: Atomoxetine
problems: Carries a boxed warning in United States — for heart harm

fda.text: Some patients may experience transient episodes of light-headedness, dizziness or syncope. Orphenadrine may impair the ability of the patient to engage in potentially hazardous activities such as operating machinery or driving a motor vehicle; ambulatory patients should therefore be cautioned accordingly.

examples.title: Orphenadrine Versus Baclofen in Treatment of Muscle Cramps in Cirrhotic Patients

summary: According to official warnings, Orphenadrine can cause brief spells of light-headedness, dizziness, or syncope (fainting), which can make driving or operating machinery dangerous [5]. In tests from a small computer program rather than human trials, the medicine received a low risk score for liver harm and a high risk score for heart harm [M]. Drugs with similar chemical features include Medifoxamine, which was removed from the market in France and Morocco due to liver injury, and Atomoxetine, which has a boxed warning in the United States for heart injury [3][4].
